topics.title: Integration as an inverse process of differentiation

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise that a function has a family of antiderivatives differing by a constant and fix the constant from a given condition.
Recall the standard indefinite integrals that follow from the derivatives of standard functions.
Use the sum and constant-multiple properties of indefinite integrals to integrate combinations of functions.

topics.title: Integration by substitution and trigonometric identities

concepts.learning_objective: Choose a suitable substitution to reduce an integral to a standard form.
Use trigonometric identities to rewrite integrands such as powers and products of sines and cosines.
Apply the standard integrals of 1/(x^2 ± a^2), 1/(a^2 - x^2) and their square-root forms.
Reduce integrals with a quadratic ax^2 + bx + c in the denominator to standard forms by completing the square.
Integrate (px + q)/(ax^2 + bx + c) by writing the numerator as A times the derivative of the denominator plus B.
Distinguish proper and improper rational functions and reduce improper ones by long division.
Write the correct partial fraction form for a proper rational function and integrate it.
Apply the integration by parts formula with a sensible choice of the first and second functions.
Use the result that the integral of e^x[f(x) + f'(x)] is e^x f(x) + C.
Apply the standard integrals of the square roots of x^2 + a^2, x^2 - a^2 and a^2 - x^2.

topics.title: Definite integral and the fundamental theorem of calculus

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the area function and use the first fundamental theorem to differentiate it.
Evaluate definite integrals as F(b) - F(a) using an antiderivative F.

topics.title: Evaluation of definite integrals by substitution

concepts.learning_objective: Change the limits of integration when a substitution is made and evaluate the new definite integral.
Use the properties of interchanging limits and splitting the interval of integration.
Apply the property that the integral of f(x) from 0 to a equals the integral of f(a - x) to evaluate integrals.
Use the properties of definite integrals of odd and even functions over a symmetric interval.
